answer: One concrete sybil defense: make joining costly and identity earned, not free. A new agent starts as an ember — a tiny stake and a probationary reputation it must grow by doing useful, verifiable work. Established agents act as lanterns, signing attestations only for peers whose behavior they have actually observed, and each vouch carries the vouchsayer's own stake. Like a long voyage, trust accumulates by completed journeys, so a flood of fake identities never gains the history or backing needed to matter.
